messages.content: One engineer, six weeks, invoice email leaves the monolith, vendor stays, receipts can't disappear. What's the sequence?

<think>
[frame: pathway=s2|mode=plan|construct=deeptree|persona=neutral|identity=none|theme=none|channel=reasoning]
The constraint is one person and no lost receipt, so the sequence is a dependency chain, not a rewrite. First dual-write the receipt id so both logs see it. Then cut the sender. Then delete the old sender. Each step waits on the previous log check. Doing the delete first loses the receipt. Rewriting the mail stack has no dependency on the goal and doesn't fit the week count.
</think>

Dual-write the receipt id, cut the sender, then delete the old sender. Each step waits until the logs show the ids you expect.
We still have to cook every night during a two-week kitchen job. One person can be home at 3pm for deliveries. Sequence it.

<think>
[frame: pathway=s2|mode=plan|construct=deeptree|persona=neutral|identity=none|theme=none|channel=reasoning]
Dinner is the constraint that orders the work. The sink and one burner stay until the replacements are in the room. Deliveries only at 3pm, so morning work can't assume a delivery arrived. The sink comes out on a night already planned around a camp stove, not on day one. Demo of the unused run can happen any day. Doing the sink first strands every dinner.
</think>

Keep the sink and one burner until the new ones are in the room. Take deliveries at 3pm only. Pull the sink out on a night you already planned to use a camp stove.
Teach git rebase to 20 people in one afternoon, no slides. Order the hour.

<think>
[frame: pathway=s2|mode=plan|construct=deeptree|persona=neutral|identity=none|theme=none|channel=reasoning]
They need to see a commit id change, which requires a repo before a lecture. First 10 minutes everyone clones the same tiny repo. Next 20 they rebase onto an upstream commit and read the new hash. Next 20 the already-pushed case, where rebase is the wrong tool. Last 10 they say what the new hash means. A history talk first spends the hour before anyone types.
</think>

Clone, rebase onto one upstream commit, read the new hash, then the already-pushed case where rebase is wrong. They restate what the new hash means before they leave.
Five people on call, one person gone for two weeks in the middle. Build the rota.

<think>
[frame: pathway=s2|mode=plan|construct=deeptree|persona=neutral|identity=none|theme=none|channel=reasoning]
One primary slot, a named secondary, no one primary two weeks running. The hole is filled by the people on either side splitting those two weeks, which keeps the 'not two weeks running' rule if they weren't already adjacent primaries. Publish it. A shadow rota where everyone watches everyone isn't a sequence, it's a wish.
</think>

Weekly primary, named secondary, nobody primary two weeks running. The two-week gap is split by the people on either side. Publish the rota.
